Enable is an equal opportunity employer, fostering an inclusive, accessible workplace that values diversity. We provide fair, discrimination-free employment, ensuring a harassment-free environment with equitable treatment. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. If you need reasonable adjustments during recruitment or in the role, please let us know. This job posting is for a current, existing vacancy.

title: Dealer Partner Support Specialist - Level 1 (United States)
description: About AutoFi AutoFi is the leading provider of digital commerce technology that powers the sales and finance experiences for the most innovative brands and dealers in automotive. The AutoFi platform enables a more transactional buying experience with $4B in funded loans processed through AutoFi annually. AutoFi’s dynamic selling platform empowers dealers to sell vehicles more efficiently and profitably, both online and in the showroom. We are funded for years of future growth and backed by investors including Crosslink Capital, Santander Holdings USA, SVB Financial Group, Ford, BMW iVentures and JP Morgan Chase. Our team is diverse - spread out across the U.S. and Canada, we have backgrounds from finance and technology as well as deep experience in all areas of the auto space. We’re empathetic, gritty, curious, and humble owners of this business and are supported by some of the biggest names in the auto and financial industries as commercial partners. We’ve never been more excited about the opportunity in front of us to help transition the auto industry from offline to online. If changing a trillion-dollar industry sounds exciting, we’d love to hear from you. For more information, visit www.autofi.com. About the Role Reporting to the Manager, Partner Support Services, the Dealer Partner Support Specialist is responsible for supporting the ongoing operational health, configuration, and functionality of AutoFi's products and services for our Dealership and Dealer Group partners. Acting as a key point of contact and subject matter expert following implementation, this role responds to partner inquiries, manages program adjustments, troubleshoots issues, and works collaboratively with internal teams and external vendors to ensure programs function as intended and continue to meet evolving business needs. Partner Support Services plays a key role in operating as the first line of support for all of AutoFi’s clientele. They triage and prioritize all incoming requests, resolve general inquiries, make program settings adjustments, work with vendors to align on integrated functionality, and ensure Clients/Partners are able to connect with the appropriate resources. They monitor expected program functionality, proactively taking steps to resolve potential gaps and capitalize on enhancement opportunities. An ideal candidate will be a detail-oriented, resourceful problem solver who combines strong customer service skills with technical aptitude and a commitment to accuracy. They will be comfortable managing competing priorities, investigating issues independently, and communicating effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders in a fast paced environment. Success in this role requires accountability, sound judgement, adaptability and a proactive approach to maintaining program health and delivering an exceptional partner experience. This position includes occasional scheduled evening and weekend support coverage to accommodate Dealerships operating hours. Each member of our team is challenged to contribute in a variety of capacities across the entire organization and show their individual strengths, from product to customer experience. Responsibilities Participate in and contribute to a collaborative, accountable team environment with a culture of open communication through knowledge sharing, constructive feedback, and a willingness to support shared priorities. Develop and maintain proficiency in AutoFi's product suite, integration capabilities, and Dealer Partner use cases, providing informed recommendations to optimize program configurations and functionality. Serve as a primary point of contact for Dealer Partners, responding to inquiries, resolving issues, and managing requests professionally and efficiently in accordance with expected service levels. Maintain and optimize Dealer Partner program settings, configurations, features, and integrations, including working with JSON, XML, CSS, and Regex as needed. Independently validate completed work to ensure configuration changes are accurate, complete, and functioning as intended before considering requests resolved. Perform initial troubleshooting of configuration, integration, and functional issues as needed to identify root causes, resolve common problems, and escalate more complex issues with appropriate supporting details. Collaborate with Account Management, Product, Engineering, and other internal teams, as well as external vendors, to coordinate solutions and support evolving Dealer Partner needs. Proactively monitor Dealer Partner programs to identify functional anomalies, configuration gaps, and opportunities to improve program performance and reliability. Manage a concurrent workload of approximately 20-30 assigned requests through to resolution against expected SLAs, effectively balancing competing priorities, maintaining accurate case documentation, clear stakeholder communication, and timely follow-up through phone, email and text, leveraging specific internal and vendor communications platforms where applicable. Identify recurring issues and opportunities to improve support processes, contributing to the development of standardized procedures, documentation, and best practices, inclusive of the nuances, pros and cons of various approaches. Support first-line inquiries across AutoFi's broader Partner ecosystem as needed through phone, chat and email, leveraging available tools, including AI-assisted solutions, to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Participate in scheduled after-hours support coverage, including a minimum of one Saturday per month. Qualifications 2-3 years experience working in customer support, technical support, account management or a related customer-facing role, preferably within the SaaS environment. Strong attention to detail, with a demonstrated ability to accurately execute, validate and document work Analytical and critical thinking skills, including the ability to independently investigate issues, troubleshoot basic technical problems, and determine when escalation is appropriate. Excellent written/verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly and navigate challenging customer interactions Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing requests and meet established service expectations Technical aptitude and comfort working with software configurations, system settings, integrated applications and AI Agents A proactive, accountable approach to problem-solving, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams Flexibility to participate in scheduled evening and weekend coverage including a minimum of one Saturday per month Familiarity with automotive dealership operations, business models, and personnel responsibilities strongly preferred. Working knowledge of APIs, JSON, XML, HTML, CSS, and Regex strongly preferred Experience using Salesforce, Jira, Postman, or similar CRM, case management, and API troubleshooting tools preferred. Experience using AI-assisted tools to improve productivity, troubleshooting, or customer support workflows preferred. Compensation + $2,000 performance bonus annually Additional Information What's in it for you: - We offer full training and a competitive total rewards package along with great benefits - Medical, Dental & Vision coverage - 100% premium coverage for employee / 50+% for dependents - Flexible work hours - Remote environment - Competitive pay - Visionary leadership team - Growth opportunities within a dynamic culture - Wellness & cultural initiatives (fitness challenges, wellness webinars, virtual games, regional activities, etc.) - Up to $1K per year for employee professional development - Stock options - we are all owners! Individual compensation decisions are based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience and qualifications and local market conditions. Please note, the foregoing salary range does not reflect an employee’s total compensation package, which may include bonus, company equity, and health benefits. title: Applications Engineering Manager (Boston)
description: About Standard Bots Standard Bots is building the next generation of industrial robots -- hardware that's powerful, affordable, and designed to scale. We're the largest U.S. industrial robotics company by robots shipped, and our robots are showing up on factory floors everywhere from independent machine shops to NASA and Lockheed Martin. Someone has to make sure those robots actually work -- and someone has to build the team that makes that happen at scale. That's this role. Note: This role requires up to 25% domestic travel. You're still in the field -- just not living out of a suitcase 2-3 days a week. Also note: Like every Applications Engineer at Standard Bots, this is not a software engineering role. You are a hands-on industrial automation engineer who also happens to lead people. If you've never commissioned a robotic cell, this isn't the right seat. The Role The Applications Engineering Manager is a player-coach. You still know your way around a factory floor -- fixtures, I/O, ladder logic, robot programming, all the things -- and you use that expertise every day, both to stay sharp and to earn the respect of the team you're leading. You'll manage a team of Applications Engineers across your territory, owning their development, their workload, and the quality of every customer engagement they touch. You'll be the escalation point when installs get complicated, the person who jumps on a plane when a customer situation needs senior eyes, and the one who sets the standard for what great applications engineering looks like at Standard Bots. This is still a hands-on role. You're not managing from a desk. You're leading from the front. You'll report directly to the VP of Applications Engineering. What You'll Do Team Leadership & Development - Manage and develop a team of Applications Engineers across your territory -- setting expectations, coaching on technical and customer-facing skills, and building a team that executes at a high level - Own capacity planning and workload distribution across your team -- making sure the right engineer is on the right job and nobody is drowning - Be the technical and cultural standard-setter for your team; the bar you hold yourself to is the bar your team rises to - Conduct regular 1:1s, performance conversations, and development planning -- you invest in your people's growth, not just their output Territory & Customer Ownership - Own the applications engineering function for your territory -- from pre-sales POC support through post-install customer success - Serve as the senior technical escalation point for complex integrations, difficult customer situations, or installs that aren't going as planned - Partner closely with your Regional Sales Manager on territory priorities, pipeline, and customer strategy -- you're the technical counterpart to their commercial leadership - Maintain strong relationships with key customer accounts in your territory; they should know you by name and trust your judgment Hands-On Technical Work - Stay sharp and stay in it -- you're still designing solutions, reviewing integrations, commissioning cells, and supporting installs when the situation calls for it - Lead or co-lead technically complex or strategically important customer engagements yourself - Review and sign off on solution designs, POCs, and integration plans produced by your team - Travel to customer sites as needed -- up to 25% domestically -- for escalations, key installs, and customer relationship moments Standards & Continuous Improvement - Define and enforce the standard for how applications engineering work gets done in your territory -- documentation, handoffs, commissioning checklists, customer training quality - Feed territory-level learnings back to the broader applications engineering organization and to product and engineering teams - Help build the playbooks, templates, and training materials that make every AE on your team better and every deployment more repeatable What We're Looking For - The same trifecta as our Applications Engineers -- you're genuinely fluent across mechanical, electrical, and software: PLC programming and ladder logic, pneumatics, DC power systems, robot programming, Python scripting, CAD - 5+ years of hands-on applications engineering, systems integration, or automation engineering experience -- you've done the field work and done it well - 2+ years of people management or team lead experience -- you've led engineers, given hard feedback, and helped someone grow - Strong customer-facing presence -- you can manage a difficult customer conversation, set expectations clearly, and represent Standard Bots credibly at a senior level - Experience managing a distributed team or territory; you know how to lead people you don't see every day - Comfort with up to 25% domestic travel for escalations, key customer engagements, and team support - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline -- or equivalent hands-on experience that tells the same story Nice to Have - Prior experience with collaborative robots (UR, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, or similar) - Background scaling an applications engineering or field engineering function -- you've helped build something, not just inherited it - Experience with vision systems, force/torque sensing, or custom end-of-arm tooling - Familiarity with machine tending, palletizing, welding, or assembly automation applications Compensation and Benefits The salary range for this role is $140,000 to $180,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Senior Consultant
description: Managing pricing and rebates shouldn’t be a hassle. Enable ’s intelligent platform is built for the speed of today’s market, eliminating disconnects between pricing strategy and rebate execution. We help companies to increase profitability and simplify the complex with accurate, AI-powered insights, real-time performance monitoring, agreement optimization, and simplified rebate management. After securing $291M in Series A-D funding and acquiring Flintfox in 2025, Enable is positioned for continued, significant growth. Since the launch of our flagship product in 2016, we have been rapidly scaling our client base, product offerings, and built a team of top-tier professionals committed to reshaping the industry. Want a glimpse into life at Enable? Visit our Life at Enable page to learn how you can be part of our journey. Job Summary The position is responsible for the Implementation of Enable’s products within a chosen domain of expertise, both at the individual product and solution level across multiple customer’s environments. This requires continuously refreshed, advanced level technical knowledge within chosen technical domains, working effectively as part of multi-functional project teams. You will lead the implementation, onboarding and adoption of customers, including discovery, design, configuration, testing, validation and go live phases. Duties and Responsibilities Meets or exceeds customer expectations by implementing products that address the client’s business requirements within the ‘Scope of Work’ (SOW) agreed by Enable and the customer. Able to effectively troubleshoot technical implementation issues interacting with Enable support teams to manage product issues where necessary. Actively serves as member of the Enable project team, often as a technical lead, contributing product and solution expertise to deliver customer value Contributes to building the knowledge base within Enable technical practices and communities including lessons learned, best practices, tools, methods and learning events. Serve as a coach to associate level consultants who are actively engaged as part of the project team on assigned client engagements. Identifies customer training gaps and opportunities for Enable product or service expansion and enhancement. Proactively manages issues, escalations and anticpates project risks Acts as a go-to expert for challengine questions across various subject areas Build strong, positive working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders. Mentoring and supporting team members within the Success & Services department. Lead productive customer meetings and workshops, resolving complex support tasks, and triaging incoming customer requests independently. Adheres to all company policies, including but not limited to time and expenses, code of conduct, ethics, security and any required training available. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) Demonstrates ability to implement Enable software technology within customer environments at a complex level for the individual products of chosen domain expertise. Proven and advanced level comprehension of product capabilities and how solution design can be integrated into the customer environment. Proven ability to build strong relationships with customers, communicating effectively and ensure technical project delivery Possess advanced technology troubleshooting skills for products of chosen expertise and basic technology troubleshooting capabilities, escalating where necessary. Consistently achieves role KPI’s balancing billable time with self-development plans to ensure skills are constantly updated and in demand. Ability to effectively time manage and manage multiple customer engagements concurrently Acts as a role model for co-workers and customers by clearly communicating project status udates, risks, successes and next stages of projects Experienced in change management, to facilitate smooth customer transitions from legacy systems to Enable. Continually strives to build advanced skills. Fulfils ethics, security and compliance training and test requirements to always protect Enable’s interests and assets. Preferred Education and Experience Preferred 2+ years experience working in customer facing role in Customer Success or an enterprise software organization Related Product and Industry Certifications as required (e.g. Oracle, SAP, SQL) Annually maintained all granted internal and external technical and professional certifications to latest level as appropriate. Experience with international cross cultural teams preferred Experience handling large data sets and familiarity with tools like Python or SQL. English language written and verbally fluency required, other languages preferred Travel Our roles may require some travel, with a typical average being in the region of up to 20%. Very infrequently, however, some customers at some specific stages of their projects may request a higher percentage of travel, sometimes up to 50% or more. Compensation Additional Information Total Rewards: At Enable, we’re committed to your professional development and growth. Starting pay is determined by factors like location, skills, experience, market conditions, and internal parity. Salary/TCC is just one component of Enable’s total rewards package. Enable is committed to investing in the holistic health and wellbeing of all Enablees and their families. Our benefits and perks include, but are not limited to: Paid Time Off: Take the time you need to relax and recharge Comprehensive Insurance: Health and life coverage for you and your family Retirement Plan: Build your future with our retirement savings plan Lucrative Bonus Plan: Enjoy a rewarding bonus structure subject to company or individual performance Equity Program: Benefit from our equity program with additional options tied to tenure and performance Career Growth: Explore new opportunities with our internal mobility program Additional Perks: Training: Access a range of workshops and courses designed to boost your professional growth and take your career to new heights Pets: Bring your pets to our welcoming, pet-friendly offices According to LinkedIn's Gender Insights Report, women apply for 20% fewer jobs than men, despite similar job search behaviors. At Enable, we’re committed to closing this gap by encouraging women and underrepresented groups to apply, even if they don’t meet all qualifications. Enable is an equal opportunity employer, fostering an inclusive, accessible workplace that values diversity. We provide fair, discrimination-free employment, ensuring a harassment-free environment with equitable treatment. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. If you need reasonable adjustments during recruitment or in the role, please let us know. This job posting is for a current, existing vacancy.

title: Dealer Partner Support Specialist - Level 1 (Canada)
description: About AutoFi AutoFi is the leading provider of digital commerce technology that powers the sales and finance experiences for the most innovative brands and dealers in automotive. The AutoFi platform enables a more transactional buying experience with $4B in funded loans processed through AutoFi annually. AutoFi’s dynamic selling platform empowers dealers to sell vehicles more efficiently and profitably, both online and in the showroom. We are funded for years of future growth and backed by investors including Crosslink Capital, Santander Holdings USA, SVB Financial Group, Ford, BMW iVentures and JP Morgan Chase. Our team is diverse - spread out across the U.S. and Canada, we have backgrounds from finance and technology as well as deep experience in all areas of the auto space. We’re empathetic, gritty, curious, and humble owners of this business and are supported by some of the biggest names in the auto and financial industries as commercial partners. We’ve never been more excited about the opportunity in front of us to help transition the auto industry from offline to online. If changing a trillion-dollar industry sounds exciting, we’d love to hear from you. For more information, visit www.autofi.com. About the Role Reporting to the Manager, Partner Support Services, the Dealer Partner Support Specialist is responsible for supporting the ongoing operational health, configuration, and functionality of AutoFi's products and services for our Dealership and Dealer Group partners. Acting as a key point of contact and subject matter expert following implementation, this role responds to partner inquiries, manages program adjustments, troubleshoots issues, and works collaboratively with internal teams and external vendors to ensure programs function as intended and continue to meet evolving business needs. Partner Support Services plays a key role in operating as the first line of support for all of AutoFi’s clientele. They triage and prioritize all incoming requests, resolve general inquiries, make program settings adjustments, work with vendors to align on integrated functionality, and ensure Clients/Partners are able to connect with the appropriate resources. They monitor expected program functionality, proactively taking steps to resolve potential gaps and capitalize on enhancement opportunities. An ideal candidate will be a detail-oriented, resourceful problem solver who combines strong customer service skills with technical aptitude and a commitment to accuracy. They will be comfortable managing competing priorities, investigating issues independently, and communicating effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders in a fast paced environment. Success in this role requires accountability, sound judgement, adaptability and a proactive approach to maintaining program health and delivering an exceptional partner experience. This position includes occasional scheduled evening and weekend support coverage to accommodate Dealerships operating hours. Each member of our team is challenged to contribute in a variety of capacities across the entire organization and show their individual strengths, from product to customer experience. Responsibilities Participate in and contribute to a collaborative, accountable team environment with a culture of open communication through knowledge sharing, constructive feedback, and a willingness to support shared priorities. Develop and maintain proficiency in AutoFi's product suite, integration capabilities, and Dealer Partner use cases, providing informed recommendations to optimize program configurations and functionality. Serve as a primary point of contact for Dealer Partners, responding to inquiries, resolving issues, and managing requests professionally and efficiently in accordance with expected service levels. Maintain and optimize Dealer Partner program settings, configurations, features, and integrations, including working with JSON, XML, CSS, and Regex as needed. Independently validate completed work to ensure configuration changes are accurate, complete, and functioning as intended before considering requests resolved. Perform initial troubleshooting of configuration, integration, and functional issues as needed to identify root causes, resolve common problems, and escalate more complex issues with appropriate supporting details. Collaborate with Account Management, Product, Engineering, and other internal teams, as well as external vendors, to coordinate solutions and support evolving Dealer Partner needs. Proactively monitor Dealer Partner programs to identify functional anomalies, configuration gaps, and opportunities to improve program performance and reliability. Manage a concurrent workload of approximately 20-30 assigned requests through to resolution against expected SLAs, effectively balancing competing priorities, maintaining accurate case documentation, clear stakeholder communication, and timely follow-up through phone, email and text, leveraging specific internal and vendor communications platforms where applicable. Identify recurring issues and opportunities to improve support processes, contributing to the development of standardized procedures, documentation, and best practices, inclusive of the nuances, pros and cons of various approaches. Support first-line inquiries across AutoFi's broader Partner ecosystem as needed through phone, chat and email, leveraging available tools, including AI-assisted solutions, to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Participate in scheduled after-hours support coverage, including a minimum of one Saturday per month. Qualifications 2-3 years experience working in customer support, technical support, account management or a related customer-facing role, preferably within the SaaS environment. Strong attention to detail, with a demonstrated ability to accurately execute, validate and document work Analytical and critical thinking skills, including the ability to independently investigate issues, troubleshoot basic technical problems, and determine when escalation is appropriate. Excellent written/verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly and navigate challenging customer interactions Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing requests and meet established service expectations Technical aptitude and comfort working with software configurations, system settings, integrated applications and AI Agents A proactive, accountable approach to problem-solving, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams Flexibility to participate in scheduled evening and weekend coverage including a minimum of one Saturday per month Familiarity with automotive dealership operations, business models, and personnel responsibilities strongly preferred. Working knowledge of APIs, JSON, XML, HTML, CSS, and Regex strongly preferred Experience using Salesforce, Jira, Postman, or similar CRM, case management, and API troubleshooting tools preferred. Experience using AI-assisted tools to improve productivity, troubleshooting, or customer support workflows preferred. Compensation + 2,000 CAD performance bonus annually Additional Information What's in it for you: - We offer full training and a competitive total rewards package along with great benefits - Medical, Dental & Vision coverage - 100% premium coverage for employee / 50+% for dependents - Flexible work hours - Remote environment - Competitive pay - Visionary leadership team - Growth opportunities within a dynamic culture - Wellness & cultural initiatives (fitness challenges, wellness webinars, virtual games, regional activities, etc.) - Up to $1K per year for employee professional development - Stock options - we are all owners! Individual compensation decisions are based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience and qualifications and local market conditions. Please note, the foregoing salary range does not reflect an employee’s total compensation package, which may include bonus, company equity, and health benefits. AutoFi is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment are considered without regards to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or other protected status under all applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances. Personal Information submitted as part of your application is subject to our website privacy policy, located at https://www.autofi.com/privacy-policy/

title: Medical Director, Clinical Development(Nephrology)
description: About Jade Biosciences Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Jade’s pipeline also includes JADE201, an afucosylated anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody, as well as JADE301, an anti-IFN-β monoclonal antibody. Jade was launched based on assets licensed from Paragon Therapeutics, an antibody discovery engine founded by Fairmount. For more information, visit JadeBiosciences.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn . Role Overview We are seeking an experienced and mission-driven Medical Director in Clinical Development to lead and support clinical programs in nephrology, with a focus on rare or immune-mediated kidney diseases. This role is ideal for a physician-scientist who thrives in a small biotech environment where agility, cross-functional collaboration, and scientific leadership are essential. The Medical Director will play a key role in advancing Jade’s pipeline through clinical development. This newly created position will report to the Executive Medical Director of Clinical Development. This is a fully remote role and will require some travel. Key Responsibilities Clinical Development Lead the design, execution, and oversight of clinical trials in nephrology, including protocol development, study monitoring, and data interpretation. Serve as Medical Monitor for ongoing trials, ensuring patient safety and scientific integrity. Collaborate with clinical operations, regulatory, and biometrics teams to ensure trial success and compliance. Educate and advise clinical sites/investigators to support enrollment and optimal study conduct, including presenting at investigator meetings and/or site initiation visits, and serving as the medical point of contact for site staff questions about patient eligibility, and providing input into patient safety assessment and management Provide medical expertise and support to external partners, vendors, and contractors as required to ensure smooth program execution Communicate effectively, orally and in writing, with internal and external stakeholders regarding the assigned clinical program, including the CMO, CEO, external medical experts and others. Regulatory and Scientific Contributions Contribute to the preparation of regulatory documents (INDs, NDAs, briefing documents, etc.). Support interactions with regulatory authorities and ethics committees. Stay current with scientific literature and competitive landscape in nephrology and related fields. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner with translational science, biomarker, and commercial teams to align clinical strategy with broader company goals. Provide medical input into lifecycle planning and early market preparation. Stakeholder Engagement Begin building relationships with key opinion leaders (KOLs), investigators, and advocacy groups in nephrology. Represent the company at scientific meetings, advisory boards, and industry events. Qualifications MD (or equivalent medical degree); board certification in nephrology strongly preferred. 3+ years of experience as a nephrologist in academia or industry, and/or experience in nephrology clinical trials or rare disease programs. Experience in clinical trial design, execution, and medical monitoring. Strong clinical judgment, scientific rigor, and regulatory knowledge. Ability to work independently and thrive in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence and motivate cross-functional teams, manage a diverse set of stakeholders, and work closely with team leaders High ethical standards and impeccable integrity Exercise sound judgment in managing complex, confidential, and regulated information. Position Location This is a remote role; periodic travel to team and company events is required. The anticipated salary range for candidates for this role is $270,000 - $300,000 . The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but not limited to, relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography. As part of the I-9 verification of authorization to work in the United States, Jade Bioscience participates in E-Verify. To learn more about E-Verify please review this poster . Jade Biosciences is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Security Engineer
description: About Latent Latent is the enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform, powered by a clinical agentic engine, that enables health systems to grow their pharmacy operations and serve more patients. One engine works across the pharmacy journey to identify patients who qualify for care, improve medication access, capture eligible prescriptions and support patients throughout treatment. Latent’s platform enables more than 60 leading health systems that collectively serve an estimated 70 million people. Founded by Sriram “Sri” Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, Latent has raised $80 million from Transformation Capital, Spark Capital, Conviction, General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and others. The Role We’re building the intelligence layer of American healthcare. Our systems sit directly in critical workflows and power how clinical AI is delivered and used in practice. You’ll be working on securing all aspects of Latent’s code, cloud, AI, and IT systems. You will be partnering with all Latent employees across engineering, product, legal, and GTM to safely enable Latent employees to move quickly without sacrificing security and compliance. What You'll Do You’ll be a Security generalist, helping define, lead, and execute the roadmap in all aspects of Security. Here are some of the areas you will work in: Cloud Security Mature and harden Latent’s cloud environment from a security and compliance standpoint into a secure-by-default stance so developers can ship code with confidence and the Infrastructure team doesn’t have to worry that their next Terraform apply will put everything on the open internet. AI Security Employees at Latent use a lot of AI. Help us give all of our employees access to the latest and greatest AI-powered tools in a secure and compliant way so our agents don’t run amok and do the wrong thing. Data Security Latent’s business thrives on giving our users deep insights into their patient data, their pharmacy performance, and how our AI is performing. Help us secure our data warehouse so that our internal employees and customers get the insight they need without sacrificing our commitment to patient security and privacy. Application and Product Security Latent’s developers ship a lot of code. Help us come up with ways to automate all aspects of the SDLC from a security perspective to ensure security is built in instead of being a bolt-on afterwards. In addition, as Latent plans the next iteration of its application and agentic platform, help us come up with the right security requirements for new product features and enhancements. IT Security Help our hard-working IT folks secure Latent employee devices and applications. Automate security around IT and business applications including user lifecycle provisioning, just-in-time access, elevated access provisioning, and device hardening to ensure employees can do their job securely without thinking about security. Incident Detection and Response Help the Security team investigate potential incidents, build detections that are specific to Latent’s environment, and work with our AI-native MDR service to improve accuracy around escalated incidents. What We're Looking For You’re a builder who holds yourself and others to high standards. You can design, develop, and create security automations and workflows using AI that can scale Latent’s security team. Ownership : You don’t hand off problems or wait for someone to tell you what to do. Find our gaps, risks, and vulnerabilities and implement the solution. Bias for Action : You won’t wait for someone else to solve a problem you’re in a position to solve. A Yes Mindset: Latent’s Security team is not a no factory. While we put our foot down when the risk is high, our goal is to find creative solutions that 1) Understand what an employee actually needs and 2) That balances speed and security. Automation Mindset : You’re always looking for ways to move faster by automating repetitive or manual work. Complexity Management : You’re good at planning and building the simplest solution that gets the job done, with an eye towards the future as Latent scales quickly. You can take a complex and large product and break it down into focused, iterative steps that incrementally make our security and compliance posture better. Product Focus : You’re comfortable working closely with the customers that use Latent’s security program: Latent’s employees! You love sitting alongside folks from all areas of the company, understanding their day to day, and crafting the perfect solution for them both now and in the future. Technical Qualifications We really are looking for a little bit of a unicorn and someone who has done it all when it comes to security. If you’ve worked in multiple of these areas, this is the place for you! You aren’t afraid to use coding agents to contribute solutions directly to the code base! (You don’t have to be a coding wizard Harry, but you do need to understand basic engineering principles to give your coding agent positive feedback if it spits out the wrong solution) You’ve built out IAM workflows (Okta, SSO, SAML, JIT provisioning) to give employees just the right amount of access to get their job done You’ve designed and rolled out managed settings for AI tools and coding agents to make sure employees have a good sandbox to work in to get their jobs done with AI You have collaborated with developers to help them write secure code and secure features. You’ve helped harden AWS cloud and CI/CD environments (Think well-scoped IAM roles, hardening cloud environments to CIS standards, picking the right CSPM and driving down a findings backlog ect..) You’ve helped build and maintain a vulnerability management program all the way up the stack (Server/Container/3rd Party OSS/Custom Code) You’ve automated security and compliance requirements for MacOS and BYOD endpoints using an MDM You understand your way around a security alert, security investigation, and can write and tune detections that are relevant to Latent’s environment Nice to Have You have experience working at an early stage startup doing security You’ve worked with healthcare data before and can speak a little HIPAA You’ve participated in or built controls for SOC2 audits Why Join Latent Backed by top-tier investors including General Catalyst, Conviction, and Y Combinator Work alongside a high-caliber team building products our healthcare partners love Work on mission-critical problems at the intersection of AI and healthcare Real ownership and visibility High-impact role on a small, fast-growing team Benefits Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity Medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents Flexible PTO policy Paid parental leave Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
description: Benefits We Offer $500 first client bonus* for therapists that engage with their first client within 14 days of beginning their application. Free access to 390+ CEU courses Competitive Compensation with an estimated annual earnings range of $52,000 to $81,900 that is paid hourly for someone who works 25-35 hours on the platform each week for the full year. $650 Health Insurance Stipend: Eligibility for the Health Insurance Stipend requires a continuous commitment of 30 hours a week. Additional Benefits Work from the comfort of home (fully remote) Complete control over your schedule Free BetterHelp Membership Compensation paid weekly No insurance paneling and zero fees Additional bonuses & incentives for high performers *$500 first client bonus is only available to therapists licensed in the state of Maryland, New York, North Dakota, or Washington. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Qualifications Years of Experience: 3+ years (Required) Education: Master’s (Required) Licenses We Accept: Full Independent Clinical: LCSW, LPCC, LMFT, Psychologist, PsyD, etc. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Private practice with no doors and no overhead. Join the world's largest online therapy platform. Put simply: You provide the clinical expertise, we take care of everything else. And we mean everything else. What we offer: Consistent referrals: Full clinical caseload can be established within the first 30 days. Zero overhead: No fees are collected from the therapist, ever. Flexible schedule: You are always in control of your schedule and appointment times. Engaged clients: You are connected with clients who fit your specific areas of expertise. Then, BetterHelp provides clients with a wide variety of ways to connect with you so that they can best start their therapeutic journey: from scheduled live sessions, to shared journal entries, to audio and video messages, to clinical worksheets, to formal goal setting and tracking, and more. Autonomy over clinical decisions: You are the licensed and trained clinician. BetterHelp will defer to your clinical judgment and expertise about the most effective and clinically appropriate approach for each client. Resources to keep you connected: BetterHelp has a strong and accessible peer community of over 34,000 therapists, available to you directly through the platform. Resources to support you: Therapists on the BetterHelp platform receive a free BetterHelp account – so you can dedicate time to your own self-care! Who Should Apply: Mental health therapists looking for an easy, all-in-one technology platform for telehealth. Therapists who want to focus 100% on clinical work – not on acquiring clients, billing, support, or operations. (We handle all of that!) Counselors who want a feature-rich platform that is constantly adding new clinical tools – not just video conferencing software. Mental health counselors who want the opportunity to work with specific populations or presenting concerns. Therapists & counselors who are obsessed with privacy and confidentiality, and want a state-of-the-art technology platform with secure, encrypted phone, video, and text-based communication. Requirements: Therapists must be fully licensed by a State Board to provide therapy independently and without supervision (e.g., LCSW, LPC, LMFT, PsyD or similar credentials). NOTE: Unfortunately, if you are an intern or if you require supervision to provide therapy services, you cannot be a provider on BetterHelp at this time. Also, we are unable to accept substance abuse counselors, school counselors, registered nurses, career counselors, Christian counselors, and business coaches (unless they have an additional license as a mental health counselor). Experience counseling adults, couples, and/or teens. A private and professional environment for conducting sessions. Excellent written communication. Must have professional liability insurance. Reliable Internet connection. Currently residing in the US.

title: Staff Security Operations Specialist, LeapSec
description: Company Description Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent , our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate , the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here. Your role You will own how Workleap detects, investigates and responds to threats across Workleap and ShareGate, and you will build the AI layer that runs it. Our security tooling generates more noise than a small team can work, and too many findings are ambiguous or wrong. This role exists now to turn detection and response into a system where agents triage, enrich and investigate, and people make the calls that genuinely need judgment. It is a hands on Staff individual contributor role with no direct reports. Your impact: Build the pipeline that runs security operations end to end: integrations that pull alerts and findings out of every source tool, an agentic system that triages, enriches, correlates and drafts the investigation, and a connection into Jira that routes each result to the owning team with evidence and a fix path, so no finding is ever copied by hand. Define the trust model for those agents, deciding what they close alone, what they recommend and what always goes to a human, backed by evals and secured against prompt injection and permission abuse. Drive false positives and misrated findings out of our security tooling, so every finding that reaches a person is real and correctly prioritized. Own detection engineering end to end, written as code and mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, so coverage survives any change of platform. Lead security incident response from triage to postmortem, with agents gathering the evidence, and hold our managed detection partner to a measurable standard. Make security a partner developers want to work with, delivering findings in their workflow with clear evidence and a fix path. Your team Over the next 12 months, LeapSec is delivering two strategic bets: putting security inside product squads, with agents carrying vulnerability and detection work, and automating SOC 2 evidence so nobody gathers it by hand. You will own the detection and response side of that work: cleaning up the tooling, building the agents, and proving how much they can be trusted to do alone. LeapSec covers Security Operations and Compliance across Workleap and ShareGate. You will report to the Director of Infrastructure and Security and work daily with our Staff Application Security Specialist and security tooling team, and as needed with Infrastructure, ITX and product engineering. We are a small team with a wide mandate: we track work honestly in Jira, deliver on fixed dates, and expect people to own outcomes end to end. Our environment is Azure first, with a cloud native SIEM and XDR stack, Zscaler, Cloudflare and a managed detection partner today. We choose tools on merit and expect to keep choosing. title: Executive Director, Clinical Supply Management
description: About Jade Biosciences Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Jade’s pipeline also includes JADE201, an afucosylated anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody, as well as JADE301, an anti-IFN-β monoclonal antibody. Jade was launched based on assets licensed from Paragon Therapeutics, an antibody discovery engine founded by Fairmount. For more information, visit JadeBiosciences.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn . Role Overview Jade is developing potentially transformational, disease-modifying therapies for people living with autoimmune diseases. With three biologics programs in the clinic and multiple ongoing studies from Phase I to Phase III, we are seeking an experienced Executive Director, Clinical Supply Management to join our CMC leadership team and make sure every patient in our trials receives the right investigational product, on time. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer (Head of CMC), you will own clinical supply strategy, planning and execution for all Jade programs. You will shape and scale the Clinical Supply Management function, growing and mentoring a team of internal employees and contractors, and you will lead a global network of CMOs and logistics partners supporting complex, multi-country and multi-site studies with ambitious timelines and enrollment targets. This is a high-impact role for a self-starter who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You will work closely with Clinical Operations and Clinical Development to secure supply for every planned study, help prepare the supply chain for BLA filing, launch and commercial readiness, and contribute directly to Jade’s key corporate goals. Key Responsibilities Lead and build the function: Provide strategic and operational leadership for Jade’s Clinical Supply Management function. Further develop and scale the team through a combination of internal headcount and external partners, including recruiting, onboarding and mentoring team members and consultants. Develop robust business processes and SOP in close collaboration with the Quality function. Define the clinical supply strategy: Develop and implement the clinical supply strategy for all Jade programs, from early-stage (Phase 1/2) through late-stage (Phase 3) development, with a forward-looking view toward BLA filing, product launch and commercial readiness. Plan demand and supply: Build and maintain integrated global demand forecasts and supply plans based on protocols, enrollment projections and site activation plans. Balance drug product availability, shelf life, overage and cost, and update plans as studies evolve. Advise on potential risk and challenges to Senior Management and peer groups such as Clinical Operations and Development. Collaborate cross-functionally: Partner closely with Clinical Operations and Clinical Development on study-specific supply strategies, and with Quality, Regulatory Affairs and CMC to forecast, align and continuously update supply requirements for ongoing and future studies. Develop options and recommendations for stakeholders and senior management. Select and manage CMOs and suppliers: Select, contract and manage clinical supply CMOs, depots, couriers, logistics providers, and other critical suppliers. Set clear performance expectations and KPIs, and build strong partnerships that ensure quality, reliability and cost-effective supply. Oversee clinical supply operations: Direct labeling, packaging, blinding, cold-chain storage and global distribution for all drug product formats, including vials, pre-filled syringes and autoinjectors. Manage comparator sourcing, expiry extensions, relabeling, returns, reconciliation and destruction. Manage IRT and inventory: Define supply requirements for IRT/IxRS systems, including resupply strategies and user acceptance testing, and monitor inventory at depots and sites to prevent stock-outs and minimize waste. Ensure compliance and quality: Maintain full compliance with Jade SOPs, cGMP, GDP, GCP, ICH guidelines and applicable global regulatory and import/export requirements. Partner with Quality on batch release (including QP release for EU studies), deviations and change controls, keep the function inspection-ready, and contribute to regulatory submissions (IND, IMPD, CTA). Own the budget and reporting: Manage the clinical supply budget, and report regularly and concisely to stakeholders and senior management on inventory, supply and demand, changes and risks across all programs. Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Life Sciences, Chemical Engineering or a related field. 15+ years of progressive experience in clinical supply chain management, ideally with biologics, including significant experience leading teams. Experience in commercial supply chain management is a plus. Proven experience managing clinical supply for biologics in vials within cold-chain environments, using local and multinational CMOs; experience with pre-filled syringes and combination products such as autoinjectors highly preferred. Experience supporting multiple early- and late-stage programs, including multi-country Phase 3 studies and bridging studies for biologic combination products. Comprehensive understanding of global regulatory and import/export requirements across Europe, North America, China, Japan and Rest of World (ROW), and strong working knowledge of cGMP, GDP and GCP. Hands-on experience with IRT/IxRS systems, clinical supply forecasting tools and budget management. Demonstrated success building and scaling clinical supply functions, including hiring, onboarding and managing team members and consultants to meet critical milestones. Exceptional communication, leadership and interpersonal skills, with a track record of aligning CMC, Quality, Regulatory Affairs and Clinical teams and building trusting relationships with external CMO partners. A strategic thinker with a proven execution record, strong problem-solving skills and the ability to thrive in a complex, fast-paced clinical development environment. Position Location This is a remote role; periodic travel to team and company events is required. The anticipated salary range for candidates for this role is $280,000 - $300,000 . The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but not limited to, relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography. As part of the I-9 verification of authorization to work in the United States, Jade Bioscience participates in E-Verify. To learn more about E-Verify please review this poster . Jade Biosciences is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Clinical GTM Lead
description: About Latent Latent is the enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform, powered by a clinical agentic engine, that enables health systems to grow their pharmacy operations and serve more patients. One engine works across the pharmacy journey to identify patients who qualify for care, improve medication access, capture eligible prescriptions and support patients throughout treatment. Latent’s platform enables more than 60+ leading health systems that collectively serve an estimated 70 million people. Founded by Sri Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, Latent has raised $80 million from Transformation Capital, Spark Capital, Conviction, General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and others. The Role As Clinical GTM Lead, you will be Latent’s pharmacy subject matter expert for prospective and current customers. You’ll work with Sales on demos, clinical diligence, and executive conversations; support Partner Experience through implementations and account growth; and bring what you hear from customers back to Product. You’ll help pharmacy leaders understand how Latent fits their workflows, where it can make a difference, and how we approach clinical quality and patient safety. Your presence should give customers confidence that experienced pharmacists help build Latent and support its products. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working directly with customers and turning clinical insight into practical action. What You’ll Do Clinical sales partnership Lead the clinical portions of sales calls, product demos, diligence, and executive meetings. Address questions about pharmacy operations, medication access, and how Latent fits into existing workflows. Partner with Sales to anticipate objections, explain the product clearly to clinical and nonclinical stakeholders, and build trust through accurate, direct answers. Customer implementation and growth Work with Partner Experience to understand each customer’s workflows, support implementation decisions, and help pharmacy teams adopt the product successfully. Join strategic account conversations to identify opportunities for deeper use, retention, and expansion that serve customer and patient needs. Product insight and clinical accuracy Turn customer feedback and clinical requirements into clear recommendations for Product, balancing clinical value, operational feasibility, and business impact. Review customer-facing claims, presentations, and guidance for clinical accuracy and sound judgment around patient safety, compliance, and product positioning. Tools that help the team scale Create reusable clinical presentations, diligence responses, workflow guidance, and answers to common customer questions. Equip Sales and Partner Experience to handle recurring clinical questions confidently while knowing when to bring in deeper pharmacy expertise. What Success Looks Like Within six months: You are a trusted clinical partner on our most important sales opportunities and customer accounts, and you have built materials and processes that Sales and Partner Experience use regularly. Within 12 months: Your work has strengthened clinical confidence throughout the sales process, supported retention and expansion, and established a clear feedback loop among customers, Latent’s clinical team, and Product. What We’re Looking For A PharmD from an accredited institution and an active or recently active pharmacist license in at least one U.S. state. At least seven years of relevant experience across pharmacy practice, clinical operations, healthcare technology, or related work, including meaningful experience with pharmacy workflows. Strong understanding of medication access and the day-to-day needs of pharmacists, pharmacy leaders, and the organizations they serve. Experience working directly with customers and communicating with clinical, operational, and executive stakeholders. You can lead a detailed workflow discussion and an executive conversation with equal confidence. A record of owning clinical, operational, product, or customer outcomes, with the ability to turn clinical requirements into practical solutions. Clear writing and presentation skills. You make complex clinical topics understandable and create materials that other teams can use. Sound judgment about clinical risk, patient safety, compliance, and the claims we make about our product. Comfort learning and explaining technical and AI products, and working closely with commercial and technical teams. A hands-on, low-ego approach. You take ownership, move through ambiguity, and help the team get the work done. Nice to Have Experience at a healthcare technology, digital health, or pharmacy technology company. Experience supporting enterprise healthcare sales, strategic accounts, or technology implementations in a pharmacy organization. Familiarity with AI products or clinical decision support tools. Relationships with pharmacy executives or health system pharmacy leaders, or experience speaking at industry events. Why Join Latent Help more patients get the medications they need by improving how pharmacy teams work. Work closely with Sales, Partner Experience, Product, and our clinical team on problems that matter to customers. Shape how Latent earns clinical trust as the company grows, with the ownership to build what the team needs.

title: Senior Donor Relations Officer
description: You: The champion who turns belief in liberty into the resources to defend it. Every case PLF wins starts with someone who chose to fund the fight. You'll be that person's trusted partner. You'll get to know what drives our donors, show them the real impact of their giving, and invite them to make bold investments in freedom. Them: Bureaucrats, city councils, mayors, governors, and federal agencies stripping Americans of their rights every day. There’s a lot of government overreach out there, and it’s backed by seemingly endless resources. But fortunately, like all lumbering giants, abusive government is most vulnerable when countered by individuals who act strategically and nimbly, take calculated risks, have each other’s backs, and are confident in and passionate for the cause—the very sort of swashbucklers we employ in spades here at PLF. Us: We fight back. Pacific Legal Foundation is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the United States Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 21 litigated at the Court—including three victories last term. We also have nearly two hundred active cases across the nation. We are a next-generation public interest law firm. That means we aren’t interested in doing the same thing as everyone else. We aspire to be the best player in a constantly changing game . Here’s what you get to do in this role: The Senior Donor Relations Officer is responsible for developing and managing a portfolio of high-capacity current and prospective major gift donors, with responsibility for the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of significant philanthropic relationships supporting Pacific Legal Foundation’s mission and strategic priorities. The Senior Donor Relations Officer will develop and execute sophisticated donor strategies, build meaningful long-term relationships with donors and prospects, and secure significant new, renewed, and increased philanthropic commitments. The successful candidate will be an accomplished frontline fundraiser with exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, strong fundraising judgment, and a demonstrated record of closing significant major gifts. The position requires a highly organized, persistent, disciplined, and self-directed professional who can operate with substantial independence while collaborating effectively with PLF leadership, attorneys, and Development colleagues. Getting down to brass tacks, your specific job duties likely will include : Managing a portfolio of approximately 100 high-capacity major gift donors and prospects and achieve established fundraising, engagement, and solicitation goals. Developing and executing individualized strategies for donor qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. Personally soliciting and securing significant new, renewed, and increased gifts, including six-figure and seven-figure commitments. Building trusted, long-term donor relationships by understanding donors’ interests, motivations, and philanthropic priorities and serving as their primary PLF relationship manager. Creating meaningful donor engagement and stewardship opportunities that demonstrate the impact of philanthropy and connect donors to PLF’s litigation, policy, and strategic priorities. Strategically engaging PLF executives, attorneys, trustees, and other organizational leaders in donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. Identifying and advancing new major gift prospects and recognize opportunities for multi-year, planned, blended, campaign, and other complex gifts in collaboration with Development colleagues. Maintaining a disciplined portfolio and moves management, including donor strategies, next steps, solicitation plans, revenue projections, contact reports, and accurate CRM records. Contributing to Development team strategy and serve as a resource to colleagues on complex donor relationships and major gift opportunities. The ideal candidate will have: 8+ years of professional fundraising experience, including substantial frontline major gift experience. A demonstrated record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing significant major gifts, preferably including six and seven figure commitments. Exceptional interpersonal, listening, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and communicate complex ideas clearly and compellingly. Strong strategic judgment, initiative, organization, and personal accountability, with the ability to operate independently in a results-oriented environment. Proficiency with fundraising CRM systems and disciplined portfolio and moves management practices. A willingness to travel up to 50% throughout the United States, with a heavy focus throughout California, to meet with donors and prospects. A sincere appreciation for PLF’s mission Preferred experience. Previous experience with a pro-liberty organization, legal advocacy organization, public policy organization, or similar mission-driven institution is a plus. Experience with Salesforce or a comparable fundraising CRM is also preferred. General information: Pacific Legal Foundation identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that will benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, we battle for freedom in the nation’s courts and the court of public opinion. As a national nonprofit organization, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California and Arlington, Virginia, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. You may work from any of our offices or request to work remotely, although strong preference will be given to California-based candidates. Salary range and benefits: This is a full-time, permanent position. PLF is committed to recruiting and retaining the highest-quality talent available nationwide, and we offer a total compensation package that includes a competitive salary, medical and dental insurance, and employer-paid retirement savings. We take work-life balance seriously through our generous paid leave and flextime policies. To learn more about the starting salary range and benefits options, please apply. How to apply: Qualified candidates should submit the following application materials: Résumé Cover letter detailing the candidate’s sincere interest in Pacific Legal Foundation, its mission, and the Senior Donor Relations Officer position

We have two product lines: Workleap Agent , our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate , the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here. Your role At Workleap, turning AI experiments into production capabilities is already part of how we build products and improve internal operations. Our Data team brings strong data engineering and science foundations; this role adds dedicated production AI engineering. As a Senior AI Developer, you'll design, build, and operate the AI systems and agentic workflows that connect foundation models to our data, tools, and applications, and you'll set the technical direction for how we do it well. Your impact: Ship production AI systems and agentic workflows that deliver measurable value in Workleap's products and internal operations. Own the production quality of those systems: observability, testing, security, and cost built in from the start. Turn evaluation evidence from Data Scientists into engineering improvements, so we know whether a system is getting better or worse. title: Associate Director, Development Outsourcing
description: About Jade Biosciences Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Jade’s pipeline also includes JADE201, an afucosylated anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody, as well as JADE301, an anti-IFN-β monoclonal antibody. Jade was launched based on assets licensed from Paragon Therapeutics, an antibody discovery engine founded by Fairmount. For more information, visit JadeBiosciences.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn . Role Overview As the Associate Director of Development Outsourcing, you will play a key role in supporting the sourcing and strategic management of Jade's external vendors. This role will partner closely with Development Operations and study teams to support vendor sourcing, contracting, governance, and the development of strong vendor relationships across clinical development programs from Phase I through Phase IV. The successful candidate will work cross-functionally to drive effective execution, support issue resolution, and contribute to continuous improvement of Development Outsourcing processes. This newly created role will report to the Director, Development outsourcing. This is a fully remote role and will require occasional travel. Key Responsibilities Serve as the primary Development Outsourcing lead for assigned studies and programs, partnering closely with cross-functional study teams and external vendors to ensure successful execution of outsourcing activities. Implement outsourcing strategies and plans established by Development Outsourcing leadership while independently managing day-to-day vendor-related activities for assigned studies. Provide outsourcing expertise and recommendations to study teams regarding vendor selection, contract strategy, oversight, and issue resolution. Ensure outsourcing deliverables, timelines, and decisions are executed efficiently and aligned with study objectives. Lead vendor sourcing and evaluation activities in support of Development Programs, including preparation of RFI/RFP materials, proposal review, bid defense coordination, comparative analyses, and recommendation development. Lead the development, negotiation, and execution of vendor agreements, including Confidentiality Agreements, Master Service Agreements, Statements of Work, Change Orders, rate cards, Letters of Intent, and other vendor-related agreements. Partner with Legal, Finance, and study teams to drive contract execution and resolve business or operational issues impacting study startup or execution. Act as the day-to-day outsourcing representative for assigned vendors and studies, proactively identifying and resolving operational issues, risks, and decisions. Escalate significant risks, relationship concerns, performance issues, or strategic decisions to Development Outsourcing leadership while driving follow-through on agreed actions. Support vendor governance activities by preparing materials, tracking actions, monitoring performance metrics, and ensuring commitments are executed. Monitor vendor performance and support implementation of corrective and preventive actions when needed. Partner closely with Development Operations, Clinical Quality Assurance, Legal, Finance, and other stakeholders to ensure effective vendor oversight and execution. Support vendor qualification, audit readiness, inspection preparedness, and oversight activities in collaboration with Clinical Quality Assurance. Maintain documentation related to vendor selection, contracting, governance, performance management, and issue resolution. Contribute to continuous improvement of Development Outsourcing processes, tools, templates, and best practices. Operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment by balancing urgent issues, strategic priorities, and routine responsibilities across multiple concurrent activities. Exercise sound judgment and independent decision-making when addressing operational challenges, while recognizing when leadership engagement or escalation is required. Demonstrate initiative and accountability by driving decisions, resolving obstacles, and ensuring commitments are completed. Qualifications 8-12 years of biotechnology, pharmaceutical, CRO, or contract research experience with significant experience in Development Outsourcing, Clinical Operations, Vendor Management, or a related function. Strong understanding of clinical development and outsourced service delivery models across Phases I-IV. Demonstrated experience leading vendor sourcing initiatives, RFP processes, bid defenses, contract negotiations, and vendor oversight activities. Experience negotiating and managing Master Service Agreements, Statements of Work, Change Orders, and other vendor-related contracts. Proven ability to independently manage complex outsourcing activities across multiple studies and stakeholders. Strong business judgment, organizational skills, and ability to prioritize effectively in a dynamic environment. Ability to identify risks, make timely decisions, and drive resolution of issues with limited direction. Strong communication, negotiation, influence, and relationship management skills. Experience collaborating effectively within cross-functional and matrixed organizations. Position Location This is a remote role; periodic travel to team and company events is required. The anticipated salary range for candidates for this role is $175,000 - $190,000. The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but not limited to, relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography. As part of the I-9 verification of authorization to work in the United States, Jade Bioscience participates in E-Verify. To learn more about E-Verify please review this poster . Jade Biosciences is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Programmatic Advertising Specialist - BENELUX
description: Programmatic Advertising Specialist (Dutch Speaking) Publisher Success | Amsterdam, Netherlands (Onsite) | Full Time | Permanent About Refinery89 Refinery89 is a Dutch AdTech company headquartered in Madrid, working with premium publishers worldwide to optimize programmatic advertising performance. Through advanced, data-driven technology, we help publishers maximize advertising revenue, improve monetization efficiency, and gain greater transparency across their advertising operations. Our international team brings together specialists in programmatic advertising, publisher monetization, technology, and account management to deliver measurable results for our partners. Interest in working directly with publishers and developing long-term business relationships. Nice to Have Experience with Google Ad Manager or other advertising platforms.
